distribution.title:
The purpose of data collection and generation in the SwyCard project is to develop and analytically validate a non-invasive, sweat-based diagnostic platform for pediatric and neonatal health monitoring, advancing the technology readiness level from TRL 3 to TRL 4.

Data will be generated to:

Establish standardized protocols for non-invasive sweat sample collection;

Quantitatively analyze biochemical and metabolic biomarkers in sweat and paired blood samples using LC-MS;

Develop sweat–blood correlation models and define clinically relevant biomarker panels;

Establish pediatric sweat biomarker reference intervals;

Build an internal sweat biomarker reference database supporting future diagnostic development and commercialization.

The data originate from sweat and blood samples collected from pediatric and adult subjects, associated clinical metadata, experimental LC-MS measurements, and derived analytical and statistical outputs.

dmp.description: SwyCard is a clinical testing method for neonates that detects biomarkers in sweat using a non-invasive sweat collection patch. This innovation enables early, accessible health monitoring, benefiting patients, reducing healthcare costs, and advancing science and biotech. The current solution is at TRL 3 (proof-of-concept established in a lab setting), and the project aims to bring it to TRL 4, with a validated prototype tested in a relevant laboratory environment. The overall aim of the project is to develop a novel, non-invasive, sweat-based health testing platform and to establish biomarker reference ranges to support the development of new clinical tests for pediatric patients.
dmp.ethical_issues_description: The project involves sensitive health data and commercially valuable data, requiring GDPR compliance, ethical approval, and IP protection.
